As someone that has worked in industry a little bit I knew instantly the issues you were having with your pyramid and that 3D printing was the solution. Injection molding has a high initial cost, but low per unit cost, while 3D printing has a low initial cost, but high per unit cost. Also, if you were smart you probably would have hired someone who knows what they are doing on fiver to design the pyramid and your hook for you instead of spending a full day on it. It likely would have only cost you like $50 to hire someone to design those both. Honestly, that’s a job that I could see AI being able to do fairly shortly if it can’t already. A simple project like that is something AI tends to do well. You would likely have to help it a little, but you could have built the whole thing with it. Like first prompting it for the measurements of each piece after telling it how big you wanted it and the basic shape. Then once you had that you could give it prompts to make each file using those measurements. AI isn’t the best at figuring out the logic of the process, but it is good at all the boring stuff, which is kind of the point of your video.
